The largest bone in the human body is the femur.

Regarding the effectiveness of Myofascial Release (MFR) therapy as described: MFR is generally considered an effective adjunctive treatment for myofascial pain syndrome and related musculoskeletal conditions. By applying gentle, sustained pressure to the fascia, therapists aim to release restrictions, improve tissue elasticity, and reduce pain. Clinical evidence suggests it can help increase range of motion and decrease muscle tension, particularly when combined with other therapeutic interventions. However, its effectiveness can vary depending on the individual patient, the severity of the condition, and the skill of the practitioner. It is often most beneficial as part of a comprehensive rehabilitation plan rather than a standalone cure.
